title: Banjo players: Gallier, Lorenzo Staulz and the Marreros
summary: Miller discusses banjoists he worked with and compares triple strokes with straight four.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, let's talk on about some of the other three parts. Okay, right out. What about banjo players? Who were some of the good ones?

Well, the one who played with me was pretty good, I know, Gallier. He played with me. And Lorenzo Starr played with me. Tom Benton played with me. And I wouldn't say that it was the best, Dick. I couldn't say that because, you know, a whole lot of them playing a lot of banjo around here. So I just couldn't say it was the best. But I know I liked the bloody name better than them Gallier. I liked his Gallier.
What kind of a fella was he, Gallier?
Gallier was a big tall fella, drinked a lot. Well, they say he was fussy, but he wasn't fussy with us.
He didn't get salty or anything.

Not when I'm about with me. And I heard he got killed. I didn't know what it was all about. But they say he didn't like that little fella or something. I don't know what it was all about. Yeah. I wasn't here.
Well, I think the guy had to do it.
Yeah, I heard of him.
Couldn't help it. Well, what kind of style did Gallier play on the banjo? Did he play?
Gallier? Well, I say he used to do what you call a lot of triples. You know, like that made the banjo triple. They had good wrists. Good wrists for that.
So they wouldn't play just a straight four in those times?

Well, they'd do it at a certain amount of time, you know? Mm-hmm. Then he'd get to doing that. Well, you know, banjos took so low. Mm-hmm. See? Well, that's what I'm talking about. They used to take so low.

Mm-hmm. Well, when they were playing in the rhythm section down here in the old times when you first got here, who would play straight four? Would there be any banjo players that just would plong, plong, plong, plong? Well, yeah, that was Lorenzo.
He did that.
Lorenzo Stahl just played a straight four.
Yeah, straight chord.
Mm-hmm. Straight. Never make nothing but straight. On the order of Lawrence Marrero? Uh-huh. You ever worked with Lawrence ever? No. No, I worked with his brother, 20 days. Yeah. Simon?
Yeah. I played with Simon.
You know what Lawrence sounded like, though. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. And it's, and Lorenzo Stahl played that way. Yeah, just right there, too.
Yeah.
What about John Marrero? John? John, the other banjo player.

Well, John, I played with him. He was pretty, he was pretty good. He could do some of the guyette stuff like that, you know. Mm-hmm. Pretty good. Well, this fellow, what you just called, he older than John. Lawrence?
I think he was the youngest. I don't know. I don't know. He just died recently, Lawrence Marrero.
Mm-hmm.
A year ago.
I know John and Simon. I know them good.
But Lawrence was just a straight-and-forth banjo player. He's the guy that was with George Lewis and Bunk, you know.
With Bunk? Yeah.
When Bunk went to New York.
